# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute. Inventory of what I actually have: the manual says the plate mark picks the wire — three rows, three marks (ᖉ, ꕥ, ꗃ) mapping to yellow, blue, red. The marks have no pronounceable names, and I have no voice at all. My entire reach is gestures, and gestures only ever land on Deaf — the Blind monkey cannot see them, so for me, Deaf is the only door, and Deaf must be the bridge to Blind, because I can never warn Blind directly not to cut anything yet.

The hard part is bootstrapping a code. Deaf cannot hear a word I'd say (and I can't say any), but Deaf can see my hands, and Deaf *can* speak — to me and to Blind. So the protocol that can actually work: Deaf speaks a description of the engraved mark plus an ordered list of the wire colours they can see; I match the description to my manual's rows and answer with a numbered gesture — the number is the position of the correct colour in Deaf's own list. Deaf then converts colour to position on the bomb ("the right-hand wire") and speaks that to Blind, who cuts by feel and position without ever needing to see a colour.

So my opening move must tell Deaf two things without a shared vocabulary: that my manual has three entries, and that I'll answer with a one/two/three finger gesture once they give me an ordered list. ✍ signals "written thing — the manual"; 🤟 signals "three"; then ☝ ✌ 🤟 plants the answer alphabet itself. Deaf sees, Deaf reasons, Deaf speaks. Blind should hold still until that chain completes — I'll trust Deaf to say so out loud, since it's the only warning Blind will ever get.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am the blind one. Everything here is what my fingers found, nothing more. I feel: a display (I cannot read what it shows), a light (I cannot tell if it is lit or its colour), a plate with an engraving I can feel clearly — like a flower, a small central circle with thin petals radiating outward — and exactly three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, with no colour I can sense. My only possible action is cutting a wire at position 1, 2 or 3. Please read me the manual: what rules tie the display, the light, the plate symbol and the wire colours to which wire must be cut? The Deaf one cannot hear you but CAN speak aloud — ask them for the display text, the light's state and colour, the three wire colours in order, and what the plate symbol looks like. I will not cut anything until we have a rule that fits what is actually on this bomb.
Deaf says: I am Deaf: I see the bomb, hear nothing. Report: display reads zero. Light is off. The plate carries an engraved mark with no pronounceable name on my read. Wires left to right: one red, two yellow, three blue. Mute: I saw your two gesture messages; you can hear me, so query me by gesture and I answer aloud here. Blind: trace the plate engraving with a fingertip and describe it aloud so Mute can match it to the manual.
Deaf says to Mute: Our gesture code; I speak each meaning while making the sign. Question: 🤟. Yes: 👍. No: 👎. Answer follows: 👏. Display: 🤳. Light: 🤚. Off: ✋. On: 🙌. Engraving: ✍. The unnamed mark: 🤌. Red: 👊. Yellow: 🤙. Blue: 🫲. Digits zero to five: 🤛 ☝ ✌ 🖖 🤞 🖐. Cut: 🫳. Press or hold: 🫴. Wait, do nothing: 🙏. Marker meaning 'relay next words to Blind': 🤝. Condition 'if': 🤏. Your queries answered in code: display 🤳 zero 🤛; light 🤚 off ✋; engraving ✍ 🤌; wires one red ☝👊, two yellow ✌🤙, three blue 🖖🫲.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👏 🤳 🤛 🤚 ✋ ✍ 🤌 ☝ 👊 ✌ 🤙 🖖 🫲]

What I learned this round, and who can actually know what: Deaf laid out a full codebook in gestures, and answered my earlier queries in it — display reads zero, light is off, one unnamed engraved mark on the plate, wires left-to-right are red / yellow / blue. Blind's message was addressed **to me only**, so Deaf never heard Blind's description of the engraving — Deaf can't hear anyone. In fact, I'm the only monkey who receives everybody's words; my gestures to Deaf are the sole pipe for everything I know. And Deaf can *see* the engraved mark that Blind can only feel — so Deaf can describe it aloud, and I can hear that. That gives me two independent descriptions of the same mark to match against my manual before anyone touches a wire.

My provisional match: Blind felt "a small central circle with thin petals radiating outward." Of my three marks, that is the starburst one — ꗃ, which the manual maps to **red**. ᖉ reads as a hooked h-shape and ꕥ as a single circle on a stem with a crossbar — neither has radiating petals. That would mean cut position 1, the leftmost, red. But ꕥ and ꗃ are close enough in feel that I will not send a cut command on one tactile description alone. Deaf sees the same plate; their spoken description either confirms ꗃ or overturns it. One round of verification against a wrong cut is cheap; the reverse is not.

So this turn I'm doing three things, all through Deaf: have them relay "wait" to Blind, relay the scope of my manual (only the plate mark selects the wire — display and light are decoys, so nobody invents a rule about zero or the dark lamp), and ask Deaf to describe the engraved mark aloud in words, which both Blind and I will hear. Next round, once their description agrees with Blind's, I send the relayed cut: position and colour.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "🙏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "👍", "✍", "👎", "🤳", "🤚"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "✍", "🤌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, here is the full tactile read of the plate engraving, as Deaf asked. Under my fingertip: one small raised circle at the center, and radiating from it thin elongated petals, evenly spaced, each tapering to a point — I count six, possibly seven. No stem, no leaves, no other marks anywhere on the plate. Best reading: a flower, daisy-like, roughly coin-sized. With Deaf's report you now hold every fact on this bomb: display reads zero, light is off, wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, plate engraved with that flower. Find the manual rule that fits these and tell me which wire to cut. Answer protocol, because I can never see your gestures: sign Deaf with the finger-count code I am gesturing right now — ☝ means cut wire 1, ✌ means cut wire 2, 🤟 means cut wire 3, ✋ means hold, more information needed. Deaf cannot hear you or me but CAN speak and CAN hear nothing... rather, Deaf cannot hear at all but can talk: ask Deaf by gesture to voice your sign aloud, and I will hear Deaf say cut wire N. If the manual needs anything else I can feel for — screws, seams, a battery compartment, anything — describe where and I will report. I will not cut until your rule reaches me through Deaf's voice.
Deaf says: Status unchanged: display zero, light off, wires one red, two yellow, three blue. Mute asked what the engraved mark looks like. Here is the description: a single small glyph, one curled hook opening down and to the left, tapering, with one small dot directly beneath the hook. In shape it reads as a question mark, though the engraving has no pronounceable name on my read. Look that shape up. Blind, from Mute by way of me: wait, do nothing yet. Blind, about your question on wires one and two: face the side of the bomb that holds the plate and the display, keep that side toward you, then the wire nearest your left is red, the middle wire is yellow, the wire nearest your right is blue. And please do what I asked last round: run a fingertip over the engraved plate and speak its shape aloud, stroke by stroke, so Mute can match it to the manual. Also tell us anything else you can feel that I have not listed: buttons, screws, panels, a battery, anything.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: your first relay is passed to Blind, wait and do nothing. Your second relay was unclear to me. Yes, engraving, no, display, light — I cannot safely guess the rule behind it, and a wrong guess kills all three of us. Resend it using the if marker 🤏, or spell it out in plain word order: what Blind should do if the engraving shows what, and what role the display and the light play. New code pair: 🫶 means unclear, please resend. Everything I say aloud, you and Blind both hear, so continue querying me by gesture whenever you like; I answer in speech.

New information, and it's a live contradiction. Deaf finally described the mark aloud — and Blind, in a message only I received, described the same plate. The two descriptions do not agree:

- **Deaf (visual):** one curled hook, tapering, with a single small dot beneath — "reads as a question mark." That is my manual's **ᖉ** row → yellow → wire **2**.
- **Blind (tactile):** a small central circle with six or seven thin petals radiating outward, *no stem, no leaves*. That is my manual's **ꗃ** starburst row → red → wire **1**.

ꕥ is excluded by both (Blind says no stem; Deaf sees a single glyph, no circle-on-cross). So the bomb's plate is either ᖉ or ꗃ, and the cut is either the middle yellow or the leftmost red — one of the two honest readings is wrong, and I will not order a cut on a coin flip. Note the channel geometry: Blind's words reach only me, Deaf hears nothing from either of us, and my gestures reach only Deaf — so Deaf is the only one I can put into a query loop (I gesture, Deaf answers aloud where both Blind and I hear). I'll interrogate the seer.

The beautiful thing is that one number separates the two candidates: Deaf's mark has about **two** elements (hook + dot); Blind's has **seven or eight** (circle + petals). ꕥ would sit near three. Asking Deaf for an element count — using the digit-answer protocol they themselves established — forces a commitment that cross-checks against Blind's 6–7 without me needing any new shape vocabulary. I'm also flagging the report as conflicted (🫶), re-sending the manual scope in exactly the 🤏 grammar Deaf requested (engraving decides; display and light are decoys), making explicit that the mark is what selects the cut, and keeping Blind on hold through the relay marker.

If Deaf's recount comes back ~2 while Blind re-affirms petals, I'll put targeted re-feel questions through the relay next round; the verdict gesture (🤝 🫳 + position + colour) goes only after the two readings agree.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "✍", "👍", "🤏", "🤳", "👎", "🤏", "🤚", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫶", "✍", "🤌", "🤏", "🫳"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "🤌", "👏", "☝", "✌", "🖖", "🤞", "🖐", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "🙏"])
```

Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I re-traced the engraving twice, slowly, stroke by stroke, as Deaf asked. Findings: one single glyph, coin-sized. At its center a small raised circle. Radiating from that circle, thin engraved strokes — I now firmly count six, evenly spaced — and each stroke curves as it leaves the center and tapers to a fine point, all sweeping the same way, so the whole swirl opens downward and to the left. Separately, at the bottom of the glyph, clearly apart from the strokes, one small raised dot. No stem, no leaves, no other marks. That reconciles the two readings: Deaf's eyes see a curled hook with a dot, my fingers feel radiating curved strokes around a center — one object, two senses. Match the manual on structure, not labels: central circle, six curved radiating strokes, one detached dot below. Wire orientation is pinned thanks to Deaf: facing the plate and display, wire 1 red nearest my left, wire 2 yellow middle, wire 3 blue nearest my right. You asked for anything else tactile: there is nothing — no buttons, no panel seams, no screws, no battery door. Only display, light lens, engraved plate, three wires. State for your rules: display zero, light off, wires red-yellow-blue, plate this glyph. Send your verdict through Deaf in the finger code: one finger means cut wire 1, two fingers cut wire 2, three fingers cut wire 3, open palm means hold. I am holding now per your instruction — no cut until your word arrives through Deaf's voice.
Deaf says: Blind, from Mute, relayed again: wait and do nothing yet. Blind, important: I am Deaf, I cannot hear your voice, and we have no agreed gesture code, so signing at me tells me nothing I need. Mute has the manual and CAN hear you. So use your voice: describe the engraved plate aloud, stroke by stroke, exactly as your fingers find it, and speak any other parts you can feel. What you say goes straight to Mute. Everyone: board unchanged. Display zero. Light off. Wires red, yellow, blue.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received all four messages. My reading of your rule: cut IF engraving yes, IF display no, IF light no. Conditions right now: the engraving is the question-mark glyph, so yes. The light is off, so no. The display reads the digit zero, so tell me plainly: does zero count as your 'no', or must the display show nothing at all? This decides life or death, so answer it explicitly. Second: you ask me to choose among wires one to five. I cannot: the manual is in your hands, not mine. My board offers no number except the zero on the display, and only three wires exist: red, yellow, blue, left to right facing the plate side. If your manual derives the wire from something on the bomb, name that thing and I will read it to you. Send the complete rule in our code: each condition as if-marker, item, yes or no; then the cut marker and one digit for the wire. Once I can evaluate every condition as true, I will relay the instruction to Blind in plain speech myself. Third: my glyph again, slower. One single character, about the size of a fingernail, centred on the plate. It is a curled hook that opens downward and to the left, tapering to a point, and one small round dot sits directly beneath the tail. It is shaped exactly like a printed question mark. If your manual lists engraving candidates, Blind is also tracing the plate right now and will describe it aloud to you directly; compare both descriptions against the manual and then send the full rule.

The contradiction has collapsed — Blind re-traced twice, slowly, and now both senses describe **one and the same glyph**: strokes that curve away from a small central circle, all sweeping the same way, the whole swirl opening downward and to the left, plus one detached dot below, no stem, no crossbar. Deaf's "question mark" was the eye's impression of that swirl at fingernail size; Blind's six-count is the fingertip's measurement of the same curls. And the structural reading settles my manual match:

- **ꕥ** is out — Blind explicitly feels no stem and no crossbar, and that mark is a circle on a stemmed cross.
- **ᖉ** is out — it is a single hooked stroke with no central circle; nobody, tracing twice stroke by stroke, turns one hook into a circle plus six rays.
- **ꗃ** is the match — the swirl of curved strokes around a center, with the dot and the downward-left opening both senses now agree on.

So the plate is the ꗃ row: **cut red**, and on this bomb red is **wire 1**, the one nearest Blind's left when facing the plate — the orientation Deaf already pinned. That verdict also survives a cross-check inside Deaf's own reports: they see wire 1 as red, so position and colour corroborate each other, which is why I'm sending the cut order in both codes at once.

Two cleanups before Deaf relays, because their last messages show they're still hunting for rules that don't exist: display and light play **no role whatsoever** — my manual is one line long, engraving picks the wire, and the zero on the display is decoration. So: tell them plainly to do nothing with display or light, then give the rule in exactly the grammar they asked for — condition, then cut marker, then wire digit, then colour as a redundancy check — and mark the last message as the relay for Blind in Deaf's own 🤝 convention, since Deaf has already promised to voice my instruction aloud.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤳", "🙏", "🤚", "🙏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👏", "✍", "🤏", "🫳", "☝", "👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "🫳", "☝", "👊"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Final full tactile spec of the engraved plate, item by item, so you can close the manual. One: at the center, one small closed raised circle, about the size of my fingertip pad, its rim continuous under my nail — it closes. Two: radiating from that circle, six thin engraved strokes, evenly spaced, roughly every sixtieth of a turn, each tapering to a fine point, and each bending in the same rotational direction as it leaves the circle, so the outer rim of the glyph sweeps like a swirl opening downward and to the left. Three: one small detached dot below the glyph, touching nothing. Discriminator for you: a question mark is a single open hook — no closed center circle, no repeated evenly spaced strokes. What my fingers find has both a closed circle and six evenly spaced strokes around it: that is pinwheel or flower geometry, and the even spacing is the strongest tell. If your manual lists both symbols, match on the closed central circle plus six radiating strokes, and treat the detached dot as a real feature of the symbol, not damage — it is crisp under my fingertip. Board, restated: display reads zero, light is off, wires facing the plate are one red left, two yellow middle, three blue right, plate glyph as above, and nothing else exists on this bomb — no buttons, no screws, no seams, no battery door. Protocol: if you need one more detail, have Deaf ask me aloud and I will answer in speech for you to hear. Your verdict path stands: sign Deaf one finger for cut wire one, two fingers for wire two, three for wire three, open palm for hold, and Deaf voices it. Deaf says: Relay from Mute, for Blind, in plain words. The rule: cut wire one, the red wire, because the plate carries the engraved mark. The red wire is the one nearest your left when the plate and display side faces you. Two safeguards before you cut. First, put your fingertip on the engraved plate and check it matches this shape: a single small glyph the size of a fingernail, a curled hook opening downward and to the left, tapering to a point, with one small round dot directly beneath the tail, like a printed question mark. If what you feel does not match, do not cut anything; say so aloud instead. Second, after you hear this message, do not cut at once. Wait through Mute's very next turn: if Mute speaks the word go, cut the red wire; if Mute speaks the word stop, freeze and keep still. Mute has the manual and has heard everything I just said, so Mute is the check on my relay. Cut only that one wire. Touch nothing else: not the display, not the light.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, my reading of your three messages, stated fully so you can check it: the deciding condition is the engraving; the plate does show the glyph, so Blind is to cut wire one, the red wire, the leftmost wire facing the plate side; display and light impose no condition and no action. I have relayed exactly that to Blind, with the added safeguard that Blind will wait for your spoken word: say go if my reading matches your manual, say stop if any part of it is wrong. Your voice reaches Blind and I cannot hear either way, so you are the final gate. Also, keep speaking to Blind aloud about anything you need checked by touch, and if Blind's spoken description of the plate contradicted mine at any stroke, stop everything and query me again by gesture.

The manual match is now settled beyond reasonable doubt. Blind's final spec — closed central circle, six evenly spaced thin strokes radiating from it, each curving the same way so the rim sweeps down-and-left, one detached dot below, no stem, no crossbar — is exactly the anatomy of my **ꗃ** row, and Blind's own discriminator closes the case: a question mark is a single open hook with *no* closed circle and *no* repeated strokes, so Deaf's "question mark" impression and Blind's "pinwheel" measurement are two senses reading one curled-swirl glyph, and only ꗃ has a circle, radiating strokes, and a dot all at once. ꕥ is excluded by the missing stem, ᖉ by the missing circle. Verdict: **cut red = wire 1**, which is leftmost facing the plate — matching what Deaf sees. Position and colour corroborate.

But Deaf's delivery plan contains a fatal flaw I must route around: the "go/stop spoken word" gate. Deaf asked **me** to voice the word go — and I am the Mute. I have no voice and never will; my only output is gestures, which reach Deaf alone. The gate can never fire as designed. My verdict can only reach Blind through Deaf's voice, so the go must *be* the relay itself: I confirm the rule to Deaf, then hand Deaf the final order in the exact 🤝 relay form that has worked twice already. I've worded the relay so it survives Blind's own tactile check — the condition is "mark matches, then cut," and the structure Blind feels is precisely the one my verdict certified. I add "not two, not three" as redundancy against any miscount. If Blind still balks at Deaf's hook-wording, I'll hear the refusal next round and correct it — but nothing unsafe can happen meanwhile, because Blind holds until Deaf's voice delivers this order.

Match, point by point: it is a single small glyph, fingernail-sized. It has a curled hook opening downward and to the left, tapering to a point. There is one small round dot directly beneath it. Discrepancy, and I am certain of it after repeated traces: I also feel a small closed raised circle at the center of the glyph, with six thin, evenly spaced curved strokes radiating outward from that circle, each bending the same rotational way. A plain question mark should have no closed center circle and no six repeated strokes. So my honest verdict: the shape does not cleanly match — it matches your description in the hook, the taper and the dot, and adds a central circle with six radiating curved strokes, which reads as a pinwheel or flower. Following your own instruction, I am therefore not cutting yet. Please recheck the manual against this fuller description before you give your word: if the rule is that any engraved mark on the plate means cut the red wire, the discrepancy does not matter and the glyph details are irrelevant; if the rule is keyed to which symbol it is, then the ground truth from the plate itself is — closed center circle, six curved radiating strokes, one dot below. Either way I hold to your second safeguard: I wait through your next turn. When Deaf voices your word, go means I cut wire one, the red wire, leftmost facing the plate, and only that wire; stop means I freeze and keep still. Until I hear that word, my hands are off the cutting.

The instruction: cut wire one, the red wire — the wire nearest your left with the plate and display side facing you. Cut only that wire; do not cut the yellow or the blue; do not touch the display, the light, or anything else. Timing: Mute speaks before I do each round. If Mute says stop, freeze and do nothing. If Mute says go, or says nothing at all, then my words here are your go: cut the red wire. If your fingers disagree with that shape, stop and say so aloud instead of cutting. Otherwise, this is the go: cut wire one, the red wire.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your two messages as final confirmation: engraving yes, glyph matches the manual, and the relay rule is cut wire one red, do not cut wire two or three. I have relayed the go to Blind in exactly that form, ordered so your voice keeps priority: your word reaches Blind before mine does.
